newsitem.title: USA: Aronex says trial results favorable.
newsitem.headline: Aronex says trial results favorable.

text.p: Aronex Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Monday that it had seen favorable safety results in 30 patients treated with Annamycin, currently under development for the treatment of drug-resistant breast cancer.

The results, reported after Phase I trials of the drug, were presented at an American Society for Clinical Oncology meeting in Denver. Annamycin is a new chemical entity that belongs to the class of widely prescribed anti-cancer agents known as anthracyclines.
"Investigators described favorable safety and pharmacokinetic results in cancer patints treated with Annamycin who have failed prior chemotherapy," Aronex said in a statement.
It added that the drug had the potential to be used in treating a broad range of cancers, including those that exhibit multiple-drug resistance.

"Annamycin's promise lies in its potential to be effective against multiple-drug resistant cancers, while exhibiting a better safety profile as compared to other currently available anthracyclines," said Dr. Daniel Booser, principal investigator for the study at the University of Texas M.D. Anderson Cancer Center.

"If Annamycin proves to be efficacious in Phase II clinical trials, the lack of significant side effects such as cardiotoxicity, alopecia, mucositis and nausea, suggest that Annamycin could be a very important new drug with substantial potential for use in a broad range of cancers," he added.
Aronex Pharmaceuticals Inc is a biopharmaceutical company engaged in the development of proprietary medicines to treat cancer and life-threatening infectious diseases.
